questiontext.text:
Determine the length of the curve whose equation is given by \( \displaystyle {@expr@}\), for \({@lower_y@}\leq y\leq{@upper_y@}\). Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

\(L=\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Let's take the derivative of the given function x with respect to y, and then plug it into the ds formula.

\(\frac{dx}{dy}={@coef1*2@}({@const@}+y)\)

\( \begin{align} ds &= \sqrt{1+[\frac{dx}{dy}]^{2}}dy \\ &= \sqrt{1+[{@coef1*2@}({@const@}+y)]^{2}}dy \\ &= \sqrt{1+{@(coef1*2)^2@}({@const@}+y)^{2}}dy \\ \end{align} \)

So, the integral giving the arc length is,

\[L= \int ds=\int_{{@lower_y@}}^{{@upper_y@}}\sqrt{1+{@(coef1*2)^2@}({@const@}+y)^{2}}dy\]

To evaluate this integral, we need to use a trig substitution

\(y={@1/(2*coef1)@}\tan\theta-{@const@} \qquad \rightarrow dy={@diff(1/(2*coef1)*tan(theta)-const)@}\)

\(y={@lower_y@}: \qquad {@const+lower_y@}={@1/(2*coef1)@}\tan\theta\) \(\qquad \tan\theta= {@1/(1/(2*coef1))*(const+lower_y)@}\) \(\rightarrow\) \( \theta\) = \(\tan^{-1}( {@1/(1/(2*coef1))*(const+lower_y)@})\) =\({@dd@}\)

\(y={@upper_y@}: \qquad {@const+upper_y@}={@1/(2*coef1)@}\tan\theta\) \(\qquad \tan\theta= {@1/(1/(2*coef1))*(const+upper_y)@}\) \(\rightarrow\)\(\ \theta\) = \(\tan^{-1}( {@1/(1/(2*coef1))*(const+upper_y)@})\) =\({@bb@}\)

So we have is in the range \({@dd@} \leq \theta \leq {@bb@}\) . This means we are in the first quadrant, then a secant is positive.

Now let’s deal with the square root,

\( \begin{align} \sqrt{1+{@(coef1*2)^2@}({@const@}+y)^{2}} & = \sqrt{1+{@(coef1*2)^2@}({@1/(2*coef1)@}\tan(\theta))^{2}} \\ & = \sqrt{1+\tan^{2}(\theta)} \\ &= \sqrt{\sec^{2}(\theta)} \\ &=|\sec\theta| \\ &=\sec(\theta) \quad \text{since, } \sec\theta > 0 \\ \end{align} \)

Therefore,

\( \begin{align} L&= \int_{@lower_y@}^{@upper_y@}\sqrt{1+{@(coef1*2)^2@}({@const@}+y)^{2}}dy\\ &={@1/(2*coef1)@} \int_{@dd@}^{@bb@}\sec^{3}(\theta) d(\theta)\\ &={@ta_1@}\\ \end{align} \)

questionnote.text:
The length of the curve whose equation is given by \( \displaystyle {@expr@}\), for \({@lower_y@}\leq y\leq{@upper_y@}\) is

\(L={@ta_1@}\)
